# Feature Flag Resolution

For `featureX`, the exact precedence order from highest to lowest is:

1. Project: `project.featureX`, when the property exists on the project object.
2. Environment: `environment.FEATURE_X`, when the property exists on the environment object. The value is `true` only when it is exactly the string `"on"`; any other present value resolves to `false`.
3. User: `user.featureX`, when the property exists on the user object.
4. Default: `defaults.featureX`.
5. Implicit fallback: `false` when the default is `null` or `undefined`.

Property presence, rather than truthiness, controls selection for project, environment, and user settings. Therefore, an explicit `false` still overrides all lower-precedence sources.

## Fixture Results

| Fixture case | Resolution trace | Final value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project value wins over every lower-precedence source | `project.featureX` exists and is `false`; environment `"on"`, user `true`, and default `true` are ignored. | `false` |
| Environment is used when project is absent | Project is absent; `environment.FEATURE_X` exists and is `"on"`, which converts to `true`; user `false` and default `false` are ignored. | `true` |
| User is used when project and environment are absent | Project and environment are absent; `user.featureX` exists and is `true`; default `false` is ignored. | `true` |
| Default is used when every explicit source is absent | Project, environment, and user are absent; `defaults.featureX` is `true`. | `true` |
